passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding any other statute, any vendor that provides fraud countermeasures that are contained in and on the paper used for ballots shall be ISO 27001 certified, ISO 17025 certified or ISO 9001:2015 certified.
passages.note: Bill text sets antifraud certification standards for ballot paper itself, not a rule for verifying a voter's identity or eligibility.
Finchem voted Y on final passage of SB1057, a ballot-paper antifraud certification bill that does not address voter identity verification.
Finchem is listed as Prime sponsor of SB1057, which the Governor vetoed 06/19/2026; the bill concerns ballot-paper fraud countermeasures, not voter ID.

rows.reasoning: All three passages concern SB1057, which requires vendors supplying antifraud features printed in and on ballot paper (watermarks, holographic foil, ISO certification) to be certified; none of this sets a rule for how the government verifies a voter's identity or eligibility, which is the question this ladder orders. Per the annex's 'Ballots, not voters' hard case, rules about the ballot itself (paper, design, security marks) do not verify a voter, so every passage is adjacent and none can support a chair.
needs_source: An Arizona bill, vote, or sponsorship record where Finchem acts on a rule for what identification a voter must show to vote, or on documentary proof of citizenship at registration
